kill_fact: The catalyst is REAL and PENDING -- I overturn the prior pass on that point, see corrections -- but the asymmetry is dead at $22.94 on two of the three REFUTED triggers, and the thesis type is misclassified. (1) THE FLOOR IS NOT A FLOOR, AND IT HAS ALREADY BROKEN ONCE. There is no contractual backstop of any kind: no deal price, no cash tender, no CVR, no appraisal or covenant. The board file's $17.50 floor was violated at $16.60 in late June 2026 (52-week low $16.60, confirmed). The replacement '$16.50 verified floor' is verified by nothing -- it is a 3.5-4x revenue multiple plus cash, ratified by a single tested low, and the file itself concedes 'nothing stops the stock going through $16.50 to the low teens.' The only hard asset value is net cash of $1,582.3m ($1,638.464m cash and short-term investments less $56.164m total debt, filed Q1 2026 balance sheet) = $2.99/share, which sits 87% BELOW spot and binds nothing. A special situation whose downside is defended only by sentiment is a directional growth-equity bet wearing event-driven clothing. (2) THE SPREAD IS GONE. At $22.94 the price sits AT the file's own probability-weighted fair value of ~$23. Risk/reward is 0.9:1 against the 2.85:1 the board underwrote at $20.49: the entry is 12% higher and the floor 6% lower. The discount this idea was underwritten on was paid out by a 38% rally BEFORE the catalyst did anything. (3) THE FLOW RUNS THE WRONG WAY -- the structural kill. The driver is tagged 'Forced_divest_flow,' a thesis type that pays when a known seller is EXHAUSTED and the price is freed. This event does the opposite: at the open on 7 August it ADDS ~77.7m shares to a ~238m float (+33% supply in one step), hands them to venture funds with a demonstrated price-blind in-kind distribution pattern, and leaves NO restriction behind afterward. The mechanism works against the position inside the very window being underwritten. Nothing about it exhausts supply: stock-based compensation near half of revenue manufactured +10.25% more shares in the last year alone (weighted-average shares 474.811m to 523.485m, filed). The expiry ends the contractual overhang, not the dilution. This is a post-event name, not a pre-event one.
corrections: PRIMARY CORRECTION -- I OVERTURN THE PRIOR SKEPTIC PASS, WHICH KILLED THIS ON A FALSE FACT. The prior shard ruled REFUTED / kill_scope 'catalyst' on the claim that the Extended Lock-Up Agreement 'DOES NOT EXIST,' that the catalyst FIRED around 7 November 2025 under the IPO 424B4 clause, and that 'no Figma 8-K was filed on 2025-08-30, which was a Saturday.' That reasoning attacked a straw man and its conclusion is wrong. The file never claimed an 8-K was FILED on 30 August 2025; it claimed the agreement was ENTERED on 30 August 2025 and DISCLOSED on 3 September 2025. The 8-K of 3 September 2025 (accession 0001579878-25-000026, document fig-20250903.htm) is in the prior shard's OWN six-filing list, which mislabelled it as Item 2.02 earnings only and missed the lock-up disclosure carried in the 8-K body alongside the q225pressrelease.htm exhibit. Its contents are confirmed: on 30 August 2025 Figma entered an Extended Lock-Up Agreement with holders of approximately 54.1% of outstanding Class A Common Stock, releasing in earnings-triggered tranches -- 17.5% (~38.9m) after the quarter ending 30 September 2025, a further 20% (~44.4m) after the following quarter, a further 27.5% (~61.1m) beginning at the commencement of trading on the second trading day after earnings for the quarter ending 31 March 2026, and the remainder (~77.7m) on the earlier of the second trading day after the quarter ending 30 June 2026 or 31 August 2026, when the Extended Lock-Up Period ends. Both the IPO lock-up AND the extended lock-up are real: the 424B4 lock-up did lapse in November 2025, and a SEPARATE voluntary contract re-locked 54.1% of Class A through August 2026. The prior pass found the first and concluded the second was fabricated. DECISIVE CORROBORATION FROM THE PRIOR SHARD'S OWN EVIDENCE: it cites Index Ventures VI (Jersey) LP's Form 4 for period 2026-05-18. Q1 2026 earnings were released after the close on Thursday 14 May 2026; the second trading day after is Monday 18 May 2026 -- the exact release date of the 27.5% tranche. If the lock-up had fully expired in November 2025, there is no reason Index would have distributed on precisely that day. The tranche mechanism is observed firing as written. CATALYST STATUS PENDING_HARD IS CORRECT and the date is right: Figma's press release of 15 July 2026 sets Q2 2026 results after the U.S. close on Wednesday 5 August 2026; first trading day after is Thursday 6 August, second is Friday 7 August 2026, ahead of the 31 August backstop. No slippage, no amendment. CORRECTION 2 (material, and it CUTS AGAINST the position): the file UNDERSTATES how much squeeze fuel is already burned. It cites short interest falling from 78.17m 'a month ago' to 66.09m, but 78.17m is the 15 June 2026 settlement and the file SKIPPED the 30 June 2026 peak of 84.50m (44.4% of float). The true cover is 84.50m to 66.09m = -18.4m shares (-21.8%), not -15.5%. The buyer today is later in the cover than the file admits. CORRECTION 3 (material): the residual overhang is larger than the 'roughly 90 million shares' the file attributes to Index (53.1m) and Hamid (37.1m). Founder Dylan Field's stake and the Sequoia entities are additional and are not on any clock once 7 August passes. The prior shard put these at ~78.9m and ~34m respectively; I flag the direction as confirmed but those two figures as NOT independently verified in this pass and they should not be carried as fact without a check of the 13D/A and Reed Form 4. CORRECTION 4 (minor): percent-of-float is denominator-dependent and should not be quoted as one number -- 27.75% (238.19m float), 33.16% (Finviz), 44.4% (30 June settlement); days-to-cover 2.93-3.15, not 2.9. CORRECTION 5 (minor): the path was not the clean one-way 38% rally implied -- the stock reached ~$23.65 on 13 July, FELL 16% in the week of 20-24 July on AI-competition fear, then rose 8.64% on 27 July to $22.94. It is roughly flat to mid-July; the level conclusion holds but the tape is far more two-sided. CORRECTION 6 (minor): consensus price target is $31.00 (median $32.50, high $38, low $22), not the $30.40 cited. CORRECTION 7 (minor): TTM GAAP net loss is ~$1.465bn on the filed quarters, not ~$1.40bn. WATCH ITEM: the file says management guided Q2 above a ~$330m street. Consensus has since drifted toward the top of the $348-350m guide, so the 5 August print is now a bar set at or above management's own number -- optionality converted into risk. FORENSICS THAT SURVIVED INTACT, all checked against filed statements: Q1 2026 revenue $333.439m vs $228.199m (+46.1%); cost of revenue $19.452m to $68.666m (+253%); gross margin 91.48% to 79.41%, a 12.1pp collapse in twelve months; GAAP net loss $142.401m; FCF $88.6m at 27% margin; NDR 139%; TTM revenue $1.161bn. The business quality and the margin deterioration are exactly as described. The bull's franchise case is honest -- it is the STRUCTURE of the trade, not the company, that fails. WHAT WOULD REVIVE THIS: the file's own re-entry level is the right one. At or below $18.50 against the same $29 target the ratio restores to roughly 5:1, and the 7 August supply release is the most likely mechanism to deliver it.
